finding.title: Guard SkippedTasks.build()'s fire-and-forget prefs load with ref.mounted
finding.why: build() kicks off an un-awaited async side effect (SM-2 forbids side effects in build). _loadFromPrefs() then does `await SharedPreferences.getInstance()` and further awaits before writing `state = ...` twice, with no `ref.mounted` check (SM-4) anywhere in the method. If the provider is disposed (e.g. the user navigates off the Scheduler screen quickly) before the load resolves, the post-await `state = ...` throws Riverpod 3's UnmountedRefException — which the surrounding try/catch swallows and logs via `AppLogger.instance.error(event: 'Failed to load skipped tasks', ...)`, i.e. a routine dispose race gets misreported as a genuine load failure in production logs/Crashlytics breadcrumbs, obscuring real failures of the same code path.
finding.recommendation: Check `ref.mounted` immediately before each `state = ...` assignment in _loadFromPrefs, and return early (without logging) when unmounted, matching Riverpod 3's documented SM-4 pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: _loadFromPrefs checks ref.mounted before both `state = refs.toSet()` and `state = {}`.
A widget test that disposes the ProviderContainer/screen mid-load does not produce an AppLogger error log.

finding.title: Wrap the DB write in StudyDayConfigScreen._toggleDay with catch/log and a consistent mounted guard
finding.why: _toggleDay runs its DB lookup + db.studyDayConfigDao.upsertDayConfig(...) inside a detached `.then()` async closure with no surrounding try/catch and no caller awaiting the result — if upsertDayConfig throws (constraint violation, disk error), the failure is silently swallowed by the Future machinery with no AppLogger call and no user feedback (unlike the sync-push call three lines later, which IS wrapped in `on TutorWriteException catch`). The same closure calls `ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider)` at line 288 with no `context.mounted` check, yet the SAME method DOES check `context.mounted` before the SnackBar at line 299 just after — an inconsistent, incomplete guard that leaves the earlier call exposed to a disposed-widget race if the user navigates away quickly after tapping a day toggle.
finding.recommendation: Wrap the DB write in try/catch with an AppLogger.error call and user-facing feedback on failure; check `context.mounted` (or equivalent) before the `ref.invalidate` call, matching the guard already present for the SnackBar.
acceptance_criteria: A thrown exception from upsertDayConfig is logged via AppLogger and does not vanish silently.
ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider) is only called when the widget is still mounted.

finding.title: Delete the dead onCompleted callback chain from DailyTaskCard/GroupedDailyView/SchedulerScreen

evidence.quote:
onDismissed: () => onTaskDismissed(curriculum, i),
              onCompleted: () => onTaskCompleted(curriculum, i),

finding.why: DailyTaskCard.onCompleted is `required` (every caller must supply it) but nothing inside DailyTaskCard ever invokes `onCompleted()` — its own doc comment even admits 'Kept for call-site compatibility; invoked externally', but no external invocation exists either. The real completion-triggered refresh path is `completionCommittedProvider`, incremented by text_display_screen.dart:696 and watched by allDailyTasksProvider (scheduler_providers.dart:321) — a reactive mechanism unrelated to this callback. daily_task_card_test.dart confirms this: every test passes `onCompleted: () {}` and none assert it fires. The whole chain (DailyTaskCard's param, SchedulerScreen._TaskList's and GroupedDailyView-wiring's invalidate closures, GroupedDailyView's pass-through) is vestigial from a pre-completionCommittedProvider design.
finding.recommendation: Remove the onCompleted parameter from DailyTaskCard and GroupedDailyView, and the corresponding dead closures in scheduler_screen.dart.
acceptance_criteria: DailyTaskCard and GroupedDailyView no longer declare onCompleted/onTaskCompleted.
daily_task_card_test.dart and scheduler_screen tests updated accordingly and still pass.

finding.title: Delete or wire in the dead scheduler PaceIndicator/ProjectedCompletionText widget file
finding.why: Grepping lib/ for `PaceIndicator(` and `ProjectedCompletionText(` shows the scheduler version is instantiated nowhere in production code — only its own dedicated widget test (pace_indicator_test.dart) exercises it. The app's real pace indicator on curriculum_progress_screen.dart uses a DIFFERENT, differently-shaped `PaceIndicator` class from features/progress/presentation/widgets/pace_indicator.dart (different constructor: `pace`+`subtitleCaption` vs `paceStatus`). Two same-named top-level classes (AG-4 duplicate) strongly suggests the scheduler one was superseded and simply never deleted, along with its fully-passing but functionally pointless test file.
finding.recommendation: Delete lib/features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/pace_indicator.dart and its test, or if a scheduler-local pace badge is genuinely still wanted, rename the class to avoid the AG-4 collision and wire it into a screen.
acceptance_criteria: Only one public `PaceIndicator` class exists in lib/, or the two are clearly distinctly named.
No orphaned widget file with zero production call sites remains.

finding.title: Delete or properly @Deprecated the dead, self-documented-buggy toggleStudyDay provider

evidence.quote: ///   1. It does not push sync (no syncFacade call).
// BUG: this fires before the write completes (STUDYDAY-TOGGLE-RACE-14).

finding.why: toggleStudyDayProvider has zero call sites anywhere in lib/ or test/ (confirmed by repo-wide grep) and its own doc comment states it is dead and buggy (no sync push, plus a documented race condition already fixed in study_day_config_screen.dart's _toggleDay). Yet it is not marked `@Deprecated`, so nothing — not the analyzer, not code review tooling — stops a future contributor from wiring it up and reintroducing the documented race, since a doc-comment warning is easy to miss while an `@Deprecated` annotation surfaces as an analyzer diagnostic at the call site.
finding.recommendation: Delete the provider (it has no callers) or, if it must stay for build_runner stability as the comment claims, mark it `@Deprecated('Use study_day_config_screen._toggleDay instead — this has a known race, DNI-####')`.
acceptance_criteria: toggleStudyDay is either removed or carries an @Deprecated annotation with a Linear id.
Confirm via grep that no call sites exist before deleting.
